title: Span, unsafe code, and interop — quick overview
rememberThis: Span<T> is a ref struct: stack only, no await across it, no fields on classes.
Memory<T> is for async and stored buffers; Span is for synchronous slicing.
C# 14 adds implicit conversions among Span, ReadOnlySpan, and T[].
P/Invoke is a marshalling boundary: prefer LibraryImport, pass length with pointers, dispose native resources.
bullets: stackalloc is not a heap array; overflow the stack and you die, not just allocate.
Slice a CSV row as ReadOnlySpan<char> instead of Substring per column.
fixed pins so the GC cannot move the buffer while native code holds the address.
DllImport generates a runtime IL stub; LibraryImport generates marshalling at compile time and needs AllowUnsafeBlocks.

rows.value: Prefer Memory / ReadOnlyMemory; do not keep Span across await
